text: You just started a new role. Your manager says on day one: "Figure out what needs doing and do it — I trust you." What's your honest first reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Relieved. This is exactly the kind of environment I do well in.
options.signal: High autonomy preference, self-directed

options.label: B
options.text: Curious but a little anxious — I'll need to build my own structure quickly.
options.signal: Moderate autonomy, self-aware about needing guardrails

options.label: C
options.text: Unsettled. I'd rather understand what success looks like before I start optimizing.
options.signal: Prefers clarity and defined goals before acting

options.label: D
options.text: Concerned — I might duplicate work or miss something without more guidance.
options.signal: Prefers structured, coordinated environments

text: It's 3pm on a Thursday. You've finished everything on your list and no one's assigned you anything new. What do you actually do?

options.label: A
options.text: Look around for something that needs doing and start on it.
options.signal: Proactive, self-directed, comfortable with open space

options.label: B
options.text: Check in with a teammate to see if they need a hand.
options.signal: Collaborative by default, finds purpose through others

options.label: C
options.text: Wrap up early — you earned it.
options.signal: Task-completion oriented, clear boundary between work and rest

options.label: D
options.text: Feel vaguely uneasy until you build a new list for yourself.
options.signal: High structure-need, finds comfort in planning

text: Your company is switching to fully remote, permanently. What's your gut reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Relieved. I do better without the office — fewer interruptions, more focus.
options.signal: Introvert-leaning, strong solo-work preference

options.label: B
options.text: Mixed. I'll miss the casual run-ins, but I can make it work.
options.signal: Values in-person connection but adaptable

options.label: C
options.text: A little worried. Being around people keeps me energized and on track.
options.signal: Extrovert-leaning, environment-dependent performance

options.label: D
options.text: Fine either way — I adapt.
options.signal: High environmental flexibility, low preference strength

text: Your team has a group project due next week. No one's assigned roles. What do you actually do in the first meeting?

options.label: A
options.text: Propose a way to split the work and assign ownership.
options.signal: Coordinator, structure-builder, takes initiative

options.label: B
options.text: Listen first, then figure out where you're most needed.
options.signal: Adaptive contributor, reads the room

options.label: C
options.text: Volunteer for the piece you know you can do best.
options.signal: Independent contributor, prioritizes output quality over coordination

options.label: D
options.text: Suggest the whole group work on the hardest part together before splitting up.
options.signal: Collaborative by default, values shared understanding

text: You're mid-project and a teammate is stuck on something you could solve in 20 minutes. You're also behind on your own piece. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Stop and help them — team output matters more than your individual piece right now.
options.signal: Team-first, collective success orientation

options.label: B
options.text: Send a quick message with what you'd try, then get back to your work.
options.signal: Helpful but boundaried, values both collaboration and individual accountability

options.label: C
options.text: Finish your piece first, then offer help if they're still stuck.
options.signal: Individual-first, owns their own lane

options.label: D
options.text: Flag it to whoever's coordinating so they can decide how to handle it.
options.signal: Process-oriented, defers to structure rather than acting unilaterally

text: You do your best work when...

options.label: A
options.text: You have full ownership of something and can go deep without interruption.
options.signal: Strong independent contributor, flow-state oriented

options.label: B
options.text: There's a small, tight team and you're all in it together.
options.signal: Collaborative core, thrives on shared stakes

options.label: C
options.text: You're pulling things together from different people and making them coherent.
options.signal: Integrator/coordinator, finds meaning in synthesis

options.label: D
options.text: The structure is clear and everyone knows their role.
options.signal: Execution-oriented, performs best inside defined systems

text: Your team is stuck in a meeting that's going nowhere. No one's officially running it. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Step in and give it some direction — even if it's not your meeting to run.
options.signal: Natural leader, low threshold for stepping up

options.label: B
options.text: Wait for someone else to step up; you don't want to overstep.
options.signal: Follower-comfort, respects hierarchy and role

options.label: C
options.text: Redirect the conversation with a specific question to get things unstuck — without formally taking over.
options.signal: Influence without authority, leads laterally

options.label: D
options.text: Mentally check out and wait for the meeting to end.
options.signal: Disengages from unstructured group dynamics, prefers defined contexts

text: You've been asked to lead a project you didn't volunteer for. The team is solid but the brief is vague. First thing you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Set up a kickoff to align on what success looks like before anyone starts working.
options.signal: Structured leader, goal-first

options.label: B
options.text: Start on the parts you know need doing and pull people in as needed.
options.signal: Action-first leader, learns by doing

options.label: C
options.text: Ask your manager to clarify the brief before you do anything.
options.signal: Prefers clear mandate before leading, risk-averse on scope

options.label: D
options.text: Find someone on the team who seems excited and ask them to help shape the direction with you.
options.signal: Collaborative leader, distributes ownership early

text: A project you're contributing to is clearly heading toward failure. You're not the lead. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Say something directly, even if it's uncomfortable — you'd rather raise the alarm than watch it sink.
options.signal: Speaks up, comfort with conflict, high ownership beyond formal role

options.label: B
options.text: Share your concern privately with whoever is leading it.
options.signal: Indirect feedback style, defers to hierarchy while still advocating

options.label: C
options.text: Do your part as well as you can and let the lead handle the bigger picture.
options.signal: Scoped ownership, doesn't overstep role

options.label: D
options.text: Document your concerns and raise them in the retrospective.
options.signal: Process-oriented, prefers structured feedback channels

text: You and a teammate disagree on the right approach, and the deadline is two hours away. What do you actually do?

options.label: A
options.text: Make the call yourself and move — you can explain later if asked.
options.signal: Decisive, self-reliant, fast mover

options.label: B
options.text: Quickly poll the rest of the team and go with the majority.
options.signal: Consensus-seeker, distributes ownership of the call

options.label: C
options.text: Go with whatever's safest for the deadline, even if it's not the best option.
options.signal: Risk-averse, deadline-driven, pragmatic

options.label: D
options.text: Escalate to whoever owns the decision and wait for their call.
options.signal: Defers to authority, uncomfortable with unresolved disagreement

text: You're asked for a recommendation on something important, but you only have about 60% of the information you'd want. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Give your recommendation with your current read and flag the uncertainty clearly.
options.signal: Acts on imperfect information, transparent about confidence level

options.label: B
options.text: Ask for more time to fill the gaps before you commit.
options.signal: Deliberate, information-first before deciding

options.label: C
options.text: Give two or three options and let whoever asked choose.
options.signal: Avoids single-point ownership, presents range

options.label: D
options.text: Give a provisional answer and say you'll revise it once you have the rest of the picture.
options.signal: Iterative decision-maker, comfortable with rolling updates

text: You made a call last week that turned out to be wrong. You find out today. What do you do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Tell the people affected right away and explain what happened.
options.signal: Accountability-first, direct communicator under pressure

options.label: B
options.text: Figure out how to fix it before you say anything — lead with the solution.
options.signal: Problem-solver first, manages optics carefully

options.label: C
options.text: Trace back how you made the decision to understand what went wrong.
options.signal: Analytical, root-cause oriented, learns before acting

options.label: D
options.text: Acknowledge it was wrong and move forward — dwelling doesn't help.
options.signal: Pragmatic, forward-focused, low self-criticism tendency

text: You're given a problem with no clear answer and no obvious starting point. What do you actually do in the first 15 minutes?

options.label: A
options.text: Start writing or sketching whatever you know, just to get something on the page.
options.signal: Action-first, tolerates ambiguity, uses externalization to think

options.label: B
options.text: Look for similar problems that have been solved before and adapt from there.
options.signal: Pattern-matcher, research-first, builds on precedent

options.label: C
options.text: Break it into smaller pieces until at least one piece is solvable, then start there.
options.signal: Systematic decomposer, comfort through structure

options.label: D
options.text: Talk it through with someone — thinking out loud is how you think.
options.signal: Collaborative problem-solver, externalizes to others

text: You're three hours into a problem and completely stuck. Nothing is working. What do you actually do?

options.label: A
options.text: Take a break and come back fresh — the answer usually shows up when you stop forcing it.
options.signal: Trusts diffuse thinking, low frustration tolerance with dead-ends

options.label: B
options.text: Try a completely different approach from scratch.
options.signal: Pivots decisively, doesn't invest in sunk cost

options.label: C
options.text: Ask someone for help, even if you're not totally sure what to ask.
options.signal: Collaborative default when blocked, low ego about needing help

options.label: D
options.text: Keep pushing — most breakthroughs happen just after you want to quit.
options.signal: Persistence-first, high frustration tolerance, grit-oriented

text: You notice something in a project that's not your area — something that seems wrong but you're not certain. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Dig into it yourself until you're sure before saying anything.
options.signal: Thorough, investigative, doesn't surface uncertainty prematurely

options.label: B
options.text: Flag it to whoever owns that area and let them look into it.
options.signal: Respects ownership boundaries, routes rather than solves

options.label: C
options.text: Bring it up in the next team meeting as a question.
options.signal: Uses group structure, patient, not urgent-reactive

options.label: D
options.text: Let it go — raising every uncertainty creates noise.
options.signal: Filters signal from noise, low tendency to over-involve self

text: You can ship something good today or something great in three days. What do you actually default to?

options.label: A
options.text: Ship today, most of the time. Done beats perfect.
options.signal: Speed-first, pragmatic, output-volume oriented

options.label: B
options.text: Take the three days, most of the time. I'd rather be known for quality.
options.signal: Quality-first, reputation-sensitive, depth over throughput

options.label: C
options.text: Depends entirely on context — I don't have a default here.
options.signal: Situational, resists generalizations about own values, context-adaptive

text: A colleague gets credit for work you did most of. No one else knows. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Let it go — the work happened and that's what matters.
options.signal: Impact-over-credit, low recognition need

options.label: B
options.text: Mention it to them privately — not to make it a big deal, just to name it.
options.signal: Direct but low-conflict, values honesty over harmony without escalating

options.label: C
options.text: Find a natural moment to make your contribution visible to others.
options.signal: Strategically manages own visibility, values recognition but avoids direct confrontation

options.label: D
options.text: Feel annoyed but do nothing — not worth the awkwardness.
options.signal: Avoids conflict, internalizes frustration

text: You're asked to put your name on a report that's accurate but leaves out something important. What do you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Add the missing piece yourself, even if it complicates the narrative.
options.signal: Integrity-first, willing to absorb friction for completeness

options.label: B
options.text: Ask whoever assigned it to include the context before you sign off.
options.signal: Advocates through proper channels, collaborative accountability

options.label: C
options.text: Leave it out — what wasn't asked for isn't your responsibility to volunteer.
options.signal: Role-bounded, limited sense of ownership beyond explicit scope

options.label: D
options.text: Ask why it was left out before deciding what to do.
options.signal: Investigates before acting, gives benefit of the doubt, curious not reactive

text: Two job offers. One pays more, has a clear role, and is stable. The other pays slightly less but is ambiguous, fast-moving, and has more upside. Which do you lean toward?

options.label: A
options.text: The stable one. Clarity and security matter to me — genuinely, not just as a fallback.
options.signal: Security-driven, prefers certainty, stability is a real priority not a compromise

options.label: B
options.text: The ambiguous one. Upside and pace are worth the discomfort.
options.signal: Growth-driven, tolerates ambiguity, bets on trajectory

options.label: C
options.text: Hard to call — but if forced, the ambiguous one.
options.signal: Leans growth but has real reservations; not fully at ease with risk

options.label: D
options.text: Hard to call — but if forced, the stable one.
options.signal: Leans stability but feels the pull of growth; not fully at ease with safety

text: Five years from now, which would feel like a bigger failure — being great at one specific thing, or having never gone deep on anything?

options.label: A
options.text: Never going deep. I want to be the person others come to for something specific.
options.signal: Depth-seeker, specialist identity

options.label: B
options.text: Being too narrow. I'd rather know enough about a lot to connect things others can't.
options.signal: Breadth-seeker, generalist identity, finds value in synthesis

options.label: C
options.text: Both, honestly — I want both and I don't think they're actually opposed.
options.signal: Resists either/or framing, high ambition across axes

text: Would you rather be the person who builds the thing, or the person who leads the team that builds it?

options.label: A
options.text: Build the thing. I'd lose something real if I moved too far from the work itself.
options.signal: IC-track preference, craft identity, maker at core

options.label: B
options.text: Lead the team. The leverage and the human side of it is what I find most interesting now.
options.signal: Management-track preference, interested in multiplying through others

options.label: C
options.text: I want both. I'm most energized when I'm close to the work and shaping the direction.
options.signal: Player-coach preference, high-autonomy senior IC or founding-team type

text: Tell me about a time you had to deliver difficult news to someone at work or school. What did you say, and how did it go?
Think of a time you misunderstood someone, or they misunderstood you, and it caused a real problem. What happened, and how did you sort it out?
Tell me about a time you had to convince someone of something they really didn't want to hear. What was your approach, and did it work?
What's one thing about how you work that you wish people understood sooner?
What does a genuinely good day at work look like for you — not a perfect day, just a good one?
